newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha soars, eyes on Aramco term tender.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha soars, eyes on Aramco term tender.

text.p: Naphtha prices soared in late Friday afternoon Tokyo trade due to a surge in overnight crude prices, but trading was slow ahead of the closing of Saudi Arabia's naphtha term tender, traders said.

Saudi Arabia's naphtha tender for 1997 closes at midnight Dhahran time on Friday, traders said. Open-spec naphtha for first-half December was bid at $210.00, while offers were nominally assessed at $212.00. It was quoted at $207.00/$207.75 in late Thursday trading.
Second-half December was assessed bid at $209.50, and offered at $211.50, up sharply from Thursday's $206.50/$207.25.
Inter-delivery naphtha spreads for near-term cargoes remained in contango, with second-half November/second-half December discussed at minus $1.00/even.
First-half December/first-half January and second-half December/second-half January were both discussed at plus 50 cents/$1.00.

Bidding levels for Saudi Arabian term naphtha remained unclear with most buyers planning to submit their bids in the last minute. For the second-half of 1996, the price for Ras Tanura A-180 was set at plus $3.40 over the Aramco formula.
